question: What is the innermost layer of the gastrointestinal tract wall called?
explanation: The mucosa is the innermost layer lining the lumen of the GI tract, specialized for secretion and absorption of nutrients. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which layer of the gastrointestinal tract wall is primarily responsible for peristalsis and moving food forward?
explanation: The muscularis externa contains smooth muscle layers that contract in a wave-like motion known as peristalsis to propel food along the tract. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the name of the muscular valve that prevents stomach acid from flowing back into the esophagus?
explanation: The lower esophageal sphincter sits at the junction between the esophagus and stomach, closing tightly to keep gastric acid down. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h2)

question: A patient experiences severe heartburn due to acidic contents moving backward. Which upper GI structure has failed to close properly?
explanation: Heartburn or acid reflux happens when the lower esophageal sphincter relaxes improperly, allowing stomach acid to irritate the esophageal lining. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the small intestine?
explanation: The cecum is the very first pouch-like part of the large intestine, not the small intestine. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main function of the large intestine in human digestion?

options.D: Beginning the mechanical chewing of food

explanation: As waste moves through the large intestine, excess water is reabsorbed back into the body, turning liquid chyme into solid stool. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h3)

question: What are the microscopic functional units of the liver called?
explanation: Hepatic lobules are the hexagonal structural and functional units that make up the internal architecture of the liver. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why does the liver receive blood directly from the digestive tract through the hepatic portal vein?

options.A: To produce red blood cells for the entire body
options.B: To pump oxygen-rich blood directly back to the heart
options.C: To process absorbed nutrients and filter out toxins
options.D: To collect waste to be sent straight to the lungs

explanation: The portal system allows the liver to inspect, filter, and metabolize nutrients and toxins absorbed from the intestines before they circulate systemically. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary function of the gallbladder?
explanation: The gallbladder holds bile produced by the liver and removes water to concentrate it until it is needed for digesting fats. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which two ducts join together to form the common bile duct?

options.A: Main pancreatic duct and accessory duct
options.D: Cystic duct and common hepatic duct

explanation: The cystic duct from the gallbladder merges with the common hepatic duct draining the liver to create the common bile duct. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h5)

question: What are the hormone-producing cell clusters that make up the endocrine portion of the pancreas called?
explanation: The pancreatic islets (or islets of Langerhans) contain alpha and beta cells that release hormones like insulin and glucagon into the blood. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h6)

question: How do the exocrine and endocrine functions of the pancreas differ in how they release their products?

options.A: Exocrine products go through ducts into the gut, while endocrine products go straight into the blood.
options.B: Exocrine cells produce glucose, while endocrine cells produce digestive enzymes.
options.C: Exocrine organs store bile, while endocrine organs filter toxins from the liver.
options.D: Exocrine secretions control blood pressure, while endocrine secretions digest dietary proteins.

explanation: Exocrine secretions use ducts to reach the digestive tract, whereas endocrine secretions are hormones released directly into capillaries. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T1#BMP121_U2_T1_h6)
